chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:

I asked Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about a man who has a pledge (rahn) with him but does not know whose it is among the people. He said, 'I dislike that he sell it until its owner comes.' I said, 'He does not know whose it it is among the people.' He said, 'There is either an excess or a deficiency in it.' I said, 'If there is excess or deficiency in it?' He said, 'If there is deficiency in it, it is easier for its sale; he is rewarded for what was lost from its value. And if there is excess in it, it is more severe than the current state; he sells it and keeps the excess until the owner comes.'

key_terms.الرَّهْنُ: Pledge or collateral held as security

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a pledge when the owner is unknown and the item's value has changed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides nuanced guidance on the custody of an unknown pledge, prioritizing the preservation of the owner's wealth by distinguishing between items with inherent value loss versus surplus. This ruling reflects the Shia legal principle of *ihtiyat* (precaution) in financial transactions, where retaining excess value is deemed more severe than selling with a minor loss, ensuring the custodian does not unjustly benefit from the uncertainty. The hadith underscores the ethical responsibility of the custodian to act as a faithful trustee (*amin*) until the rightful owner is identified.
